newsitem.title: UK: U.S. gasoline buyers aid oil price recovery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gasoline buyers aid oil price recovery.

text.p: Convalescing oil prices stepped up their recovery on Monday as gasoline traders in the United States showed the first sign this year of filling up ahead of the peak summer driving season.
Oil prices also found more help from concern that Iran, the world's third largest crude exporter, was back under the spotlight as an alleged sponsor of international terrorism.
London Brent crude futures for May rose 30 cents a barrel by 1545 GMT to $18.18.
"It seems like gasoline is finally beginning to show some seasonal strength," said a New York dealer.

U.S. gasoline prices traditionally rise in the spring ahead of the summer driving season but traders have been reluctant to buy heavily so far this year for fear that demand from the world's biggest consumer might prove disappointing.
On Monday, however, traders said they saw evidence of buying from refiners and the big investment funds that control speculative cash flows.

"There is likely to be some upward pressure on oil prices as refineries in the U.S. and then Europe come out of turnaround and begin to increase crude throughputs ahead of the summer driving season," said London's Centre for Global Energy Studies in a report.
U.S. gasoline stocks last week stood about three percent lower than year-ago levels.

Also helping crude was a report from the Washington Post that U.S. and Saudi intelligence authorities had linked a senior Iranian government official to a group suspected of the 1996 bombing of the Khobar U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia.

In Tehran, meanwhile, several hundred students clased with police outside the German embassy during a demonstration against last week's Berlin court ruling that Iran ordered the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Germany.
Oil dealers are watching Iranian developments closely but Europe is not expected to mimic the U.S. and place a blanket ban on trade with Tehran.
